page.h1: Plug-in (balcony) solar with a battery for an apartment (2026)
page.desc: The battery that plugs into a wall outlet is sold only in Utah, and Anker's Solarbank isn't on its US store. These are the solar battery kits renters in any state can buy, with refill hours from the included panels.
page.answer: Short answer. Plug-in solar with battery storage that feeds your wall outlet is sold for plug-and-play use only in Utah (EcoFlow STREAM Ultra, 800 W per unit), and Anker's Solarbank isn't on its US store. Elsewhere, plug your appliances into the BLUETTI AC180 + 200 W kit (1,152 Wh).

What the differences mean

  • Refill time from the included panels (battery Wh ÷ panel W, at full rated sun; real days run longer): AC180 + 200 W 1,152 ÷ 200 = 5.8 h; AC180 + 2× 200 W 1,152 ÷ 400 = 2.9 h; Elite 200 V2 + 200 W 2,073.6 ÷ 200 = 10.4 h; Elite 200 V2 + 2× 200 W 2,073.6 ÷ 400 = 5.2 h; P1800 + 400 W 1,024 ÷ 400 = 2.6 h.
  • Cost per Wh of battery (maker US stores, 2026-11-17): AC180 + 200 W $769 ÷ 1,152 = $0.67/Wh; Elite 200 V2 + 200 W $1,199 ÷ 2,073.6 = $0.58/Wh; Elite 200 V2 + 2× 200 W $1,499 ÷ 2,073.6 = $0.72/Wh; P1800 + 400 W $698 ÷ 1,024 = $0.68/Wh; AC180 + 2× 200 W $1,232 ÷ 1,152 = $1.07/Wh.
  • Energy you actually get back: OutdoorGearLab drew 950 Wh of AC from a full AC180 (950 ÷ 1,152 = 82%), and Digital Trends drew 976 Wh (85%). StorageReview drew 1.91 kWh from the Elite 200 V2 (1.91 ÷ 2.0736 = 92%) and needed 2.44 kWh to recharge it (1.91 ÷ 2.44 = 78% round trip).
  • Panel wiring: two SP200L panels in series give 2 × 24.6 V = 49.2 V open-circuit, under the 60 V limit of both BLUETTI stations.

Where a plug-in battery can feed your wall outlet, and why that's rare

A battery can only lower your bill through a wall socket if its inverter is grid-interactive. EcoFlow's STREAM Ultra is listed to UL 1741 and IEEE 1547 and has built-in anti-islanding protection. EcoFlow's US product page says that, under Utah's H.B. 340, it is "only available for sale and plug-and-play installation in Utah." EcoFlow's state tracker, dated 2026-07-04, also names Maryland. A single Ultra exports at most 800 W. Reaching the 1,200 W cap that Utah and Maryland allow takes the separate STREAM Microinverter or 2–6 Ultra units. In an outage it powers only what is plugged into its two outlets, and each appliance must have a surge power below 1,200 W. EcoFlow says pairing with DELTA power stations "will be available soon." Without net metering, EcoFlow recommends a Shelly Pro 3EM meter so the system doesn't export to the grid. The product page does not list UL 3700, the new plug-in PV standard.

Why the caps exist: PV Tech reports that a plug-in system feeds current in below the breaker, which "could overload parts of the circuit without the upstream breaker detecting it." A portable power station avoids all of this. BLUETTI says its stations and portable panels "do not feed electricity into home wiring or the utility grid." No state cap or landlord wiring approval applies. You move the fridge, router or laptop to the station.

Not recommended

The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 200 W kit is the cheapest per Wh here ($0.58), but its single 200 W panel needs about 10.4 h of full sun to refill 2,073.6 Wh. That's two sunny days for a balcony setup. For $300 more, the 2× 200 W version cuts that to 5.2 h. If you only have room for one panel, the AC180 + 200 W refills in 5.8 h.
